rules.title: A unique hostname simplifies device identification in logs and during incident response.
rules.explanation: Set a non-factory device name (not the default Xiaomi/MiWiFi/OpenWrt).
rules.impact: Event correlation and incident response are hindered.

rules.title: MiWiFi vulnerabilities (including command injection) are addressed by firmware updates.
rules.explanation: Ensure that the firmware version is pinned and the device receives updates from Xiaomi Security Center / System → Upgrade.
rules.impact: Exploitation of known CVEs (for example, CVE-2024-45348) when firmware is outdated.

rules.title: Open networks, WEP, and legacy WPA/TKIP allow interception and cracking of wireless traffic.
rules.explanation: For all APs use sae (WPA3), sae-mixed, or psk2/psk2+ccmp. none, wep, and psk (WPA) are prohibited.
rules.impact: Unauthorized access to WLAN and MITM.

rules.title: WPS is vulnerable to PIN brute-force and authentication bypass.
rules.explanation: Disable WPS (push-button/PIN) on all radio interfaces.
rules.impact: Wi-Fi compromise without knowledge of the PSK.

rules.title: UPnP allows malware to automatically open ports to the outside.
rules.explanation: Disable miniupnpd/UPnP unless there is a justified need (games/media).
rules.impact: Unauthorized inbound access to the LAN.

rules.title: Remote access to the web admin interface/SSH from the Internet sharply increases the attack surface.
rules.explanation: Prohibit management from the WAN (remote management / cloud remote / firewall ACCEPT on 80/443/22 from wan).
rules.impact: Router compromise from the Internet, RCE after authentication.
rules.scope: firewall / xiaoqiang remote / Advanced → Remote Management

rules.title: Built-in firewall/SPI is basic perimeter protection.
rules.explanation: The firewall must be active; the WAN zone input should be REJECT/DROP, with SYN flood protection enabled if the option is available.
rules.impact: Direct access to router services and LAN hosts from the outside.

rules.title: Telnet transmits credentials in cleartext.
rules.explanation: The telnet service must be disabled (nvram/bdata telnet_en≠1, no listening telnetd).
rules.impact: Interception of administrative credentials.

rules.title: SSH on Xiaomi is often enabled for debugging and must not be accessible from the WAN.
rules.explanation: Dropbear/SSH is disabled or bound only to LAN; there is no firewall ACCEPT from wan to port 22.
rules.impact: Brute force and remote root takeover.

rules.title: The factory SSID discloses the model/brand and facilitates targeted attacks.
rules.explanation: The SSID must not match patterns such as Xiaomi_*, MiWiFi_*, Xiaomi-Router*, and similar.
rules.impact: Reconnaissance and fingerprinting of the device by an attacker.

rules.title: Segmentation reduces the risk of lateral movement from guest and IoT devices.
rules.explanation: A separate guest network must be configured (guest interface/SSID).
rules.impact: Guests and IoT devices gain access to primary LAN hosts.

rules.title: Client isolation blocks communication between devices on a guest WLAN.
rules.explanation: For guest wifi-iface, isolate=1 (or equivalent AP isolation) must be enabled.
rules.impact: Compromise of neighboring guest devices.

rules.title: Uncontrolled DNS facilitates phishing and DNS hijacking.
rules.explanation: Specify explicit DNS (dnsmasq server= or wan.dns); do not leave empty or use only ISP peer DNS without a policy.
rules.impact: Redirection of traffic to malicious resources.

rules.title: Accurate time is critical for logs, certificates, and schedules.
rules.explanation: The NTP client is enabled and points to trusted time servers.
rules.impact: Incorrect logs and TLS/schedule failures.

rules.title: A DMZ fully exposes the host to the internet.
rules.explanation: The DMZ feature must be disabled unless there is an explicit production need.
rules.impact: Direct compromise of a host in the DMZ.

rules.title: Responding to ICMP from the WAN facilitates scanning and reconnaissance.
rules.explanation: There is no ACCEPT icmp rule from WAN to the device; ping from the WAN must be dropped.
rules.impact: Device discovery by scanners and DoS.

rules.title: USB shares and FTP often contain known vulnerabilities and weak accounts.
rules.explanation: Samba/vsftpd/proftpd must be disabled if file sharing is not required.
rules.impact: Data leakage and RCE via network shares.

rules.title: Each port forward expands the attack surface on the LAN.
rules.explanation: Only the minimum necessary set of redirect/DNAT rules is permitted; extras must be removed.
rules.impact: Direct access to internal services from the Internet.

rules.title: The Xiaomi factory-default LAN subnet is well known to attackers and scripts.
rules.explanation: LAN IP must not use the Xiaomi factory-default subnet range.
rules.impact: Simplified attack automation and conflicts with VPN/mesh.

rules.title: TKIP and WEP are considered broken against modern threats.
rules.explanation: encryption must not include wep/tkip/psk without AES; psk2+ccmp and sae are preferred.
rules.impact: Cryptanalysis and WLAN session hijacking.

rules.title: PMF protects against deauth/disassoc attacks on Wi‑Fi.
rules.explanation: With WPA3 (sae) or WPA2, ieee80211w=1/2 is recommended.
rules.impact: DoS and forced disconnect of clients.

rules.title: Remote management via Mi Home/MiWiFi cloud expands the trust boundary.
rules.explanation: If remote access is not needed, unbind/disable cloud remote; do not leave WAN management through an account.
rules.impact: Compromise of the cloud account equals control of the router.
rules.scope: xiaoqiang / MiWiFi App remote / cloud bind

rules.title: Enabled uart_en/boot_wait settings are typical of jailbreak/SSH unlock and increase the risk of physical access.
rules.explanation: On production devices, uart_en and boot_wait must not be enabled unless required for maintenance.
rules.impact: Local capture via UART and boot bypass.

rules.title: The WAN zone must not accept arbitrary traffic to the router itself.
rules.explanation: firewall zone wan input = REJECT or DROP.
rules.impact: Exposure of local router services to the Internet.

rules.title: A weak or missing admin password is the primary vector for taking over MiWiFi.
rules.explanation: The configuration must not indicate an empty/factory password; a root/admin password hash must be present.
rules.impact: Full control over the device and network.
